page: Amazon Web Services x2gd.xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by AWS Graviton2 processors. It features 4 dedicated physical cores built on the ARM64 architecture (ARMv8 Neoverse-N1) running at 2.5 GHz. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 16.0 GB per core. It includes a 237 GB local NVMe SSD instance store volume and operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate average capabilities for standard compute tasks, with stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU scores falling in the middle 50% tier. Memory bandwidth tests show average performance for large blocks, though small-block cached reads are relatively weak. The instance exhibits lower performance in raw computational benchmarks, with Geekbench and Passmark CPU scores ranking in the bottom 10% to 25% tiers, and single-threaded decompression tasks showing poor throughput.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the x2gd.xlarge provides a high density of memory relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require high-frequency x86 instruction sets. The inclusion of local NVMe storage and a large memory footprint makes this instance suitable for memory-intensive applications, caching layers such as Redis, and relational or non-relational database operations that benefit from high RAM-to-vCPU ratios.
